business: Rental excavators and trucks. From one sample photo, build a labeled set for return inspection: some machines with a flat tire and the rest intact, some with shattered cab glass, some with a body dent, in different scenes, plus undamaged views.

training_examples.note: Van tire collapsed at the contact patch. The mask covers the deformed rubber, not the hub.
Bus tire deflated along the ground contact. Used as a truck-class exemplar because the supplied excavator has tracks.
Shattered cab glass cropped from the supplied excavator photo.
Spiderweb fracture across a laminated windshield. Mask stays on the glass and off the mirror and dashboard.
Close-up of tempered-glass fracture. A thin border stays unmasked so the mask is not solid white.
Crushed body panel cropped from the supplied excavator photo.

unmet_reason: No undamaged photo was supplied for this equipment, so the pipeline does not invent one. Related real defect photos are still used to teach a damage class that will be painted onto the equipment that does have a clean photo.

held_out_references.reason: The deflated contact patch is only a few pixels tall, so a mask either covers the wheel or the gravel.
Excavator sidewall bubble, which is a different tire failure from a deflated tire.
Shows loose glass on a parcel shelf rather than a fractured pane.
News still of a missing rear window, too coarse to teach a dent or a crack.
Leaves and a collapsed rear window, not a readable dent or crack region.

generator: CDF AnomalyGen texture fine-tune. Defect pixels come from the reference photos, not from an image-edit model.
